## About Dr. David Shulkin

Dr. David J. Shulkin served as the ninth Secretary of Veterans Affairs (2017–2018) and previously as VA Under Secretary for Health, leading the nation’s largest integrated health system. He was CEO of Beth Israel Medical Center (New York City) and Morristown Medical Center, led the Atlantic Health System Accountable Care Organization, and founded DoctorQuality, an early consumer-facing quality-and-safety information company. His public record consistently emphasizes coordinated care, transparency and outcomes measurement — themes central to TEAM. (At the VA, for example, he directed every hospital and clinic to publicly post quality data and wait times.)

Dr. Shulkin’s record leading an ACO and the VA’s integrated system suggests he would emphasize that accountability across the full episode — not just the procedure — is where care coordination delivers value.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who is Dr. David Shulkin?

Dr. David Shulkin is the ninth U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs and a longtime value-based care leader, having previously served as VA Under Secretary for Health and CEO of Beth Israel Medical Center and Morristown Medical Center.

### Are the answers in this Q&A Dr. Shulkin's exact quotes?

No. This is a draft template of illustrative framing pending Dr. Shulkin’s review and confirmation — no statement is presented as a direct quotation from him.

### Why is Dr. Shulkin's perspective relevant to CMS TEAM?

He led an Accountable Care Organization and the VA’s integrated health system, and has a public record emphasizing coordinated care, transparency, and outcomes measurement — themes central to TEAM.

### How does CMS TEAM affect patients?

TEAM's mandatory primary-care referral requirement is designed to improve care coordination after a covered surgical episode.
